minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard Council on Aging, Monty Tech and school budget options; no override decision yet.
minutes.summary: Last scheduled department hearing night: the Council on Aging asked to raise its meal site manager to 36 hours, and Monty Tech presented its assessment and Chapter 70 formula. The school department then presented three budget versions (town manager, needs-based, level service) with health insurance, transportation and cuts discussed, and the school committee had not yet chosen cuts. The committee approved the February 13 minutes and adjourned; the override timeline was left for a Tuesday joint meeting with the select board.

public_comment.topic: Opposed the cemetery capital request, criticised cemetery commission spending and fund handling, and favoured the DPW superintendent's multi-year plan.
Asked how many Council on Aging visitors come from other towns.
Asked whether the numbers included ages 50-60 and whether non-residents are charged a fee.
Said the board members need to speak closer to the microphones so viewers can hear.
Questioned the number of school social workers given the share of students needing support; suggested outsourcing counseling.
Argued against cutting mental health staff, teachers or athletics, and said audit mandates originate federally.
Spoke for the fifth-grade band travel cut, asked for prioritised budget lists, and asked about actual-to-budget for the current year.

votes.motion: Approve the Finance Committee minutes of February 13.
Adjourn the school committee meeting (roll call).

budget_items.what_was_said: Modest increase over last year to make the meal site manager full-time and add kitchen aides; the assistant position will not be filled.
Programming line rising because entertainers and supplies cost more.
Federal entitlement grants and competitive grants offset the budget.
Total budget up a few percent, driven by net school spending requirement.
Proposes using about half of certified balance to offset assessments.
Lunenburg's required minimum contribution rises with enrollment up by two students.
Override budget plus additional Chapter 70 reallocated gives the adjusted starting point; new revenue figure from the town manager is higher.
Personnel reductions differ by version; level service salaries rise.
General ed bus contract and van pool rates rising; athletic transportation moving into the local budget.
Line reduced from the initial look as placement information became clearer.
Health insurance increase applied to monthly rates of four plans; percent change differs by budget version.
Reserve held for paraprofessional and administrator negotiations; last year's was larger.
Band travel line was cut, which a parent said will not close the overall gap.

decisions.decision: School and select board to meet Tuesday and the following Wednesday to try to finalize the school budget; the override question is expected on Tuesday.
Capital plan discussion moved to next week; next Thursday's meeting is a public hearing.
The warrant closes March 17; an article can still be placed without a final figure, though complicated.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no override decision; the school and select boards are to meet Tuesday to try to finalize the school budget, with the override question expected then.
The school department presented three budget versions (town manager, needs-based, level service) that differ in personnel reductions, and the school committee had not yet chosen cuts.
Health insurance was applied to the monthly rates of four plans, and the percent change differs by budget version; transportation lines also rise.
Monty Tech presented its FY26 assessment and Chapter 70 formula, and Lunenburg's required minimum contribution rises with enrollment up by two students.
The warrant closes March 17, and an article can still be placed without a final figure, though that is complicated; capital plan discussion moved to next week.

why_it_matters: The school budget size, and so whether residents are asked to vote on an override, was still open at this meeting, and the warrant deadline limits how long it can stay open.
Which cuts the school committee chooses (staff, athletics, band travel) was undecided, so the three versions show the range of what a final budget could change.
watch_next: Tuesday joint meeting of the school and select boards, where the override question is expected.
The March 17 warrant close, and next Thursday's public hearing, where the capital plan is to be discussed.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the school budget's main figures and on the Monty Tech grant totals, and most differences are caption misspellings of names and digits. Our minutes record no votes while the official minutes record one (approval of the February 14 minutes, 5-0-1), and our minutes carry many figures (Council on Aging, Monty Tech percentages, transportation, tuition, band travel) that the official minutes omit, so those could not be cross-checked.
